newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-CORINTHIANS BEAT SANTOS AND REPEAT FISH CELEBRATIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CORINTHIANS BEAT SANTOS AND REPEAT FISH CELEBRATIONS.

text.p: Corinthians players repeated the fish-theme celebrations which had antagonised rivals Santos in a previous meeting as they won their latest clash 4-3 in the Sao Paulo championship at the weekend.

Santos coach Vanderley Luxemburgo, whose club comes from a port city and is known affectionately as "The Fish", had publicly requested Corinthians players before the game not to carry out the celebrations.
Santos had been angered in April when Corinthians players celebrated one goal in a 3-1 win by imitating a fish floundering on the sand and another by imitating a fisherman dangling his catch.
Santos avenged the defeat by winning a second meeting 2-0 two weeks ago, when Corinthians players were pelted with objects by Santos fans in the crowd.
But Corinthians players ignored Luxemburgo's request and celebrated their second goal in Saturday night's game by imitating a fisherman throwing a net into the sea and hauling in a catch.
Corinthians won despite having midfielder Marcelinho Carioca sent off early in the second half as the four-team final stage of the competition, in which the teams play each other once, got under way.
In the other match played Sunday afternoon, Sao Paulo hammered Palmeiras 4-1 with Colombian striker Victor Hugo Aristizabal scoring a hat-trick.
Botafogo lost their unbeaten record in the Rio de Janeiro championship when they were beaten 2-0 by Vasco da Gama. Their run had lasted 22 games.
Vasco and Fluminense are level on points at the top in the third stage of the competition.

The stage winners meet Botafogo, who won the first two stages, in the final where the first team to accumulate six points take the title. Botafogo will start the final with a four-point advantage by virtue of having won two stages.
